Affiliation:: Institute of Engineering of Coimbra (ISEC), Polytechnic University of Coimbra
Techniques Used: Quantum Logic Gates (Hadamard, Pauli-X, Pauli-Z, CNOT)
Application Areas: Real-Time Anomaly Detection in Data Streams
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Automation: Integrating quantum search primitives with reinforcement learning agents to autonomously optimize complex database configurations, demonstrated by the QRLIT algorithm using Grover’s search and Q-learning for index tuning.

Model-Agnostic Stream Anomaly Explanation: Employing single-pass incremental computation and cross-correlation analysis to identify outlying attributes in high-velocity data streams, exemplified by the EXOS algorithm achieving superior F1-scores and reduced explanation latency.

Kernel-Based Defense Against Poisoning Attacks: Utilizing Radial Basis Functions and Gaussian kernel similarity matrices to detect and exclude malicious clients in Non-IID federated learning environments, as implemented in the RBF defense mechanism.

Architectural Energy-Performance Benchmarking: Conducting comparative experimental evaluations of serverless versus serverful cloud architectures using hardware-level power monitoring and TPC benchmarks to quantify energy savings and execution efficiency trade-offs.

Federated Learning Robustness via Similarity Analysis: Constructing local malicious factor metrics and similarity matrices to filter adversarial updates, ensuring global model integrity against label flipping and poisoning attacks.
Summary Description: Le Gruenwald specializes in the intersection of distributed systems, machine learning security, and quantum computing. Their research focuses on developing robust, energy-efficient, and automated solutions for big data analytics. Key contributions include the QRLIT algorithm for quantum-enhanced database tuning, the EXOS algorithm for real-time stream anomaly explanation, and the RBF defense mechanism for securing federated learning against poisoning attacks. The researcher extensively benchmarks cloud architectures, comparing serverless and serverful environments for energy efficiency and performance. By leveraging techniques such as reinforcement learning, kernel methods, and quantum algorithms, Gruenwald addresses critical challenges in data privacy, system scalability, and computational optimization across diverse application domains.
